content: The American Diabetes Association (ADA) recommends annual screening for diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) in individuals with type 1 diabetes who have had the disease for five or more years, as well as in all individuals with type 2 diabetes. The clinical presentation of symptoms in DPN can differ depending on the specific type of sensory nerve fibers that are affected. Electrophysiological testing is not typically performed as part of routine screening for DPN; however, it may be required in cases where the clinical features are atypical or unclear. Screening for DPN also involves evaluating for other potential causes of neuropathy that are unrelated to diabetes, such as deficiencies in vitamins, infections, or other chronic medical conditions.
